scope: One selected sequential external application scenario exercises PostgreSQL/MySQL operations through native Kelvo workers, metadata PostgreSQL, a private mTLS credential resolver and an AES-GCM fixture KMS.

application_boundary.entry_point: A compiled external application test process exercises API authentication, preparation and dispatch through an in-process HTTP test recorder.
application_boundary.network_paths: The production Kelvo HTTP/Arrow client and private mTLS resolver communicate across processes.
application_boundary.key_management: AES-GCM fixture KMS; no real KMS provider was exercised.

tests.counting_scope: One selected child scenario and its parent test passed; these are not two independent scenarios. Build stages are not additional test passes.

retained_failures.cause: External application module editing used the wrong working directory before fixture creation.
retained_failures.resolution: A fresh controller with corrected working-directory handling passed the same workflow.

limits: Sequential PostgreSQL/MySQL fixture acceptance; no Redis, concurrent application load, sustained application campaign or throughput measurement.
No actual KMS provider, cloud-provider account, customer deployment or production rollout acceptance.
The incoming application path uses an HTTP test recorder; this does not qualify a deployed external application HTTP server or all application routes.
The recorded lifecycle stage duration is elapsed test time, not a request-latency or capacity result.
This fixture evidence does not establish WAN behavior, multihost availability, recovery objectives or deployment sizing.
